4|Aspirin versus clopidogrel for chronic maintenance
5|monotherapy after percutaneous coronary intervention
6|(HOST-EXAM): an investigator-initiated, prospective,
7|randomised, open-label, multicentre trial
8|Bon-Kwon Koo*, Jeehoon Kang*, Kyung Woo Park*, Tae-Min Rhee, Han-Mo Yang, Ki-Bum Won, Seung-Woon Rha, Jang-Whan Bae, Nam Ho Lee,
9|Seung-Ho Hur, Junghan Yoon, Tae-Ho Park, Bum Soo Kim, Sang Wook Lim, Yoon Haeng Cho, Dong Woon Jeon, Sang-Hyun Kim, Jung-Kyu Han,
10|Eun-Seok Shin, Hyo-Soo Kim, on behalf of the HOST-EXAM investigators†
11|Summary
12|Background Optimal antiplatelet monotherapy during the chronic maintenance period in patients who undergo
13|coronary stenting is unknown. We aimed to compare head to head the efficacy and safety of aspirin and clopidogrel
14|monotherapy in this population.
15|Methods We did an investigator-initiated, prospective, randomised, open-label, multicentre trial at 37 study sites in
16|South Korea. We enrolled patients aged at least 20 years who maintained dual antiplatelet therapy without clinical
17|events for 6-18 months after percutaneous coronary intervention with drug-eluting stents (DES). We excluded
18|patients with any ischaemic and major bleeding complications. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive a
19|monotherapy agent of clopidogrel 75 mg once daily or aspirin 100 mg once daily for 24 months. The primary endpoint
20|was a composite of all-cause death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, stroke, readmission due to acute coronary
21|syndrome, and Bleeding Academic Research Consortium (BARC) bleeding type 3 or greater, in the intention-to-treat
22|population. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT02044250.
23|Findings Between March 26, 2014, and May 29, 2018, we enrolled 5530 patients. 5438 (98·3%) patients were randomly
24|assigned to either the clopidogrel group (2710 [49·8%]) or to the aspirin group (2728 [50·2%]). Ascertainment of the
25|primary endpoint was completed in 5338 (98·2%) patients. During 24-month follow-up, the primary outcome
26|occurred in 152 (5·7%) patients in the clopidogrel group and 207 (7·7%) in the aspirin group (hazard ratio 0·73
27|[95% CI 0·59-0·90]; p=0·0035).
28|Interpretation Clopidogrel monotherapy, compared with aspirin monotherapy during the chronic maintenance
29|period after percutaneous coronary intervention with DES significantly reduced the risk of the composite of all-cause
30|death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, stroke, readmission due to acute coronary syndrome, and BARC bleeding
31|type 3 or greater. In patients requiring indefinite antiplatelet monotherapy after percutaneous coronary intervention,
32|clopidogrel monotherapy was superior to aspirin monotherapy in preventing future adverse clinical events.

35|Introduction
36|After
37|percutaneous
38|coronary
39|intervention
40|(PCI),
41|guidelines recommend an initial 6-12 months of dual
42|antiplatelet therapy (DAPT), which is decided on the basis
43|of various factors, including clinical presentation (acute
44|coronary syndrome vs chronic coronary syndrome).1,2
45|After this period, indefinite maintenance of single
46|antiplatelet therapy is indicated for secondary prevention
47|of atherosclerotic cardiovascular events. Aspirin, a
48|cyclooxygenase pathway inhibitor, is the most widely used
49|antiplatelet agent and is recommended as standard
50|therapy in patients after PCI.3 The evidence for this
51|recommendation is based on collective analyses of
52|trials done several decades ago that showed benefit
53|of aspirin for secondary prevention of cardiovascular
54|disease.4,5 However, recent trials in the primary prevention
55|setting found little or no benefit in the prevention of
56|vascular events for aspirin and showed that aspirin might
57|be associated with an increased bleeding risk, including
58|intracranial and gastrointestinal bleeding.6-8 Clopidogrel,
59|an adenosine diphosphate-receptor blocker, is recom
60|mended as an alternative in patients who do not tolerate
61|aspirin therapy.9 One previous trial in 1996 reported
62|that clopidogrel might have potential benefits in patients
63|with atherosclerotic vascular disease, such as reducing
64|cardiovascular events with a reduced incidence of gastro
65|intestinal complications.10 However, the trial did not
66|specifically address the post-PCI population and was not
67|done in an era when drug-eluting stents (DES) or high-
68|intensity statins were available. A few registry-based

4|The trial protocol was approved by the institutional
5|review board at each participating site and all patients
6|were required to provide written informed consent at the
7|time of enrolment and randomisation. This study was
8|done in accordance with the standards specified in the
9|International Council for Harmonization Guidelines
10|for Good Clinical Practice and the principles of the
11|Declaration of Helsinki.
12|Randomisation and masking
13|In each participating centre, patients were randomly
14|assigned by a web-based application (MRCC IWRS
15|System; software configuration, Apache 2, PHP 5, and
16|mysql 5) developed by the MRCC (Seoul, South Korea),
17|without blocking or stratification methods. Patients who
18|met all the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion
19|criteria were randomly assigned in consecutive order
20|to either the clopidogrel group (75 mg once daily) or
21|aspirin group (100 mg once daily) in a ratio of 1:1
22|(figure 1). This study used a web-based electronic case
23|report form with the Pharmaco-epidemiology and
24|Clinical Trial Application X (PhactaX), which was
25|developed by the MRCC. When patients previously
26|using potent P2Y12 inhibitors were randomly assigned to
27|the clopidogrel group, clopidogrel 600 mg loading was
28|recommended for ticagrelor users, while prasugrel
29|users switched to clopidogrel 75 mg without a loading
30|dose. Participants and study investigators were not
31|masked to the assigned group.
32|Procedures
33|Participants received either clopidogrel (75 mg once
34|daily) or aspirin (100 mg once daily) orally. Clinical
35|follow-up was scheduled at 12 months and 24 months
36|(each with a window of plus or minus 3 months). Any
37|additional visits were at the discretion of attending
38|physicians. On each visit, active surveillance was done
39|for any adverse clinical events, along with the assessment
40|of adherence to the study drug.
41|Outcomes
42|The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause death,
43|non-fatal myocardial infarction, stroke, readmission due
44|to acute coronary syndrome, and major bleeding
45|complications during the 24-month follow-up period.
46|Major bleeding was defined as Bleeding Academic
47|Research Consortium (BARC) type bleeding of least 3.
48|The individual components of the primary endpoint,
49|revascularisation, and minor gastrointestinal complica
50|tions were analysed as secondary endpoints at 24 months.
51|Interim analysis was not planned and was not done
52|during the follow-up duration. Post-hoc secondary com
53|posite endpoints, including the thrombotic composite
54|endpoint (defined as cardiac death, non-fatal myocardial
55|infarction, ischaemic stroke, readmission due to acute
56|coronary syndrome, and definite or probable stent
57|thrombosis) and any bleeding (defined as BARC type ≥2
58|bleeding), were analysed. Detailed definitions of each
59|clinical event are described in the appendix (pp 13-18).
60|The vital status of all patients was cross-checked through
61|the National Health Insurance Service system of South
62|Korea and the South Korea National Statistics System.
63|The definite cause of death was confirmed by the
64|recorded data classified by the International Classification
65|of Disease, 10th Revision, Clinical Modification codes.
66|Additionally, all source data were checked for at least
67|80% of the patients in all centres. All serious adverse
68|events, primary endpoints, and secondary endpoints
69|were monitored on site.
70|Statistical analysis
71|The working hypothesis of our study was that clopidogrel
72|75 mg once daily would be superior to aspirin 100 mg
73|once daily as a chronic maintenance monotherapy agent.
74|The sample size calculation was based on the assumption
75|that the event rates of the primary endpoint at 24 months
76|would be 9·6% for the clopidogrel group and 12·0% for
77|the aspirin monotherapy group. The specific assumptions
78|and calculations are reported in the appendix (pp 11-12).
79|With a sampling ratio of 1:1 and an estimated rate of
80|follow-up loss as 5% in each group for 24 months,

14|Results
15|Between March 26, 2014, and May 29, 2018, 5530 patients
16|who were event free for 6-18 months after PCI and
17|successfully received the intended duration of DAPT
18|were enrolled from 37 centres. Among these patients,
19|5438 (98·3%) patients were successfully randomly
20|assigned to aspirin monotherapy (2728 [50·2%]) or
21|clopidogrel monotherapy (2710 [49·8%]; figure 1).
22|During the follow-up period, 35 (0·6%) patients used a
23|different antiplatelet regimen from that of the allocated
24|group, nine (0·2%) patients withdrew informed con
25|sent, and 91 (1·7%) patients were lost to follow-up.
26|Ascertainment of the primary endpoint was complete in
27|5338 (98·2%) patients and vital status cross-checked in
28|all patients who were randomly assigned.
29|The baseline characteristics of the total population are
30|shown in table 1 and the appendix (p 19). The two groups
31|were well balanced for demographic, clinical, and
32|procedural characteristics, and non-trial-related medica
33|tions. The mean age was 63·5 years (SD 10·7) and
34|4054 (74·5%) patients were male and 1384 (25·5%) were
35|female. The clinical diagnosis at the time of PCI was
36|stable angina in 1389 (25·5%) patients, unstable angina
37|in 1934 (35·5%), non-ST segment elevation myocardial
38|infarction in 1054 (19·4%), and ST segment elevation
39|myocardial infarction in 933 (17·2%). Angiographically,
40|955 (18·3%) had three-vessel disease, 272 (5·0%) had
41|left main disease, and the mean number of stents used
42|for treatment was 1·5 (SD 0·8). The median time from
43|PCI to randomisation was 382 days (IQR 357-422). The
44|DAPT regimen before randomisation was mainly aspirin
45|plus clopidogrel (4430 [81·5%]). The allocated treatment
46|discontinuation rates (for less than 3 months) in the
47|two groups were similar (281 [5·1%] vs 272 [4·9%]).
